concerns.text: The plan generates synthetic node coordinates via Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) on the graph‑distance matrix (see “Generate synthetic coordinates via MDS when missing (FR‑011)”). Because MDS derives positions from the topology itself, Euclidean distance is highly correlated with graph distance, so the ‘geographic proximity’ construct is conflated with topological proximity. This threatens construct validity: the measured effect of λ may simply reflect the underlying degree‑distribution rather than a genuine spatial effect.

The transmission probability uses βᵢⱼ = β₀·exp(‑λ·dᵢⱼ) where dᵢⱼ are Euclidean distances from the MDS‑generated coordinates. Since those coordinates are topology‑derived, the spatial decay parameter λ does not isolate an independent spatial factor, leaving a confound between topology and distance. The null model randomises coordinates but does not break the inherent topology‑distance relationship, so the permutation test may not adequately control for this confound.

The design fixes 50 Monte‑Carlo runs per (β₀, λ) configuration. No formal power analysis is provided; the justification (“Monte‑Carlo standard error ≤ 0.07”) is insufficient for detecting modest effect sizes (e.g., Cohen’s d ≈ 0.3). This raises a risk of Type II error, especially when the spatial effect may be subtle on synthetic data.
